source: NHTSA Vehicle Crash Test Database (public domain, US government)
summary: The RIGHT oblique: RMDB 2,490.7 kg at 90.46 km/h into a 2012 Camry (1,751.5 kg), 15 deg, 35 % overlap on the right front (report p.6, p.8). Films 1000 fps (camera 9's caption says 100 fps, against the table's 1000), onboard 500 fps; first contact at frame 50 (onboard 25). The car gets more lateral velocity than in the left tests (dv 15.9 m/s at 28 deg off its -X at 150 ms, body axes; no yaw sensor). The front end is bent toward the car's left: the far end of the bumper beam ends 294 mm FORWARD (B1), crush 579 mm at C5, beam 635 mm at B9, right wheelbase -80 mm, left +34 mm. Proposed Rubble setup: camry-oblique-right-mdb214.json (the mirror of the left stand-in).
timing: t0_frame: the film frame (0-based, as the sheets stamp it; the burned-in 'Frame' is 1-based) whose burned-in time is within 0.5 ms of 0, the lab's first contact; ms = (frame - t0_frame) * 1000 / fps_film to within that.
